title: 「Scarcely ... when ...」倒裝句

omissions: Every numbered Important Rule and Benefit is retained as a separate Chinese-primary card. Where the PDF has no complete English counterpart, the English explanation is a faithful editorial translation.
The source filename is numbered 224; it is assigned system ID ss225 because the source set contains two distinct PDFs labelled 201.

formula: Scarcely + had + subject + past participle + when + subject + past simple

formulas.formula: Scarcely + had + subject + past participle + other information + when + subject + past simple + other information

example: Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions.
exampleZh: 老師話音剛落，學生就開始發問。

examples.en: Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions.
examples.zh: 老師話音剛落，學生就開始發問。
examples.highlight: Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions.

meaning.zh: 這個句型表示第一件事情剛剛完成，第二件事情便幾乎立即發生。

rules.zh: 放在句首時，必須使用倒裝語序 普通語序： The teacher had scarcely finished speaking when the students started asking questions. 倒裝語序： Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions. 必須把 had 放在主語前面： Scarcely + had + the teacher + finished... 不可寫成： Scarcely the teacher had finished...
rules.en: When Scarcely begins the sentence, invert the first clause by placing had before the subject.

rules.zh: 第一部分使用過去完成時 句型的第一部分是： had + past participle 例如： ● had finished ● had opened ● had left ● had begun ● had been completed
rules.en: Use the past perfect, had + past participle, in the first clause.

rules.zh: 第二部分通常使用過去式 Scarcely had the bell rung when the students left the classroom. ● 第一件事：had rung ● 第二件事：left
rules.en: Use the past simple in the second clause after when.

rules.zh: 與 when 配搭 正確： Scarcely had the meeting begun when the fire alarm sounded. 錯誤： Scarcely had the meeting begun than the fire alarm sounded. 請記住： ● Scarcely ... when ... ● Hardly ... when ... ● No sooner ... than ... 本練習只接受 Scarcely ... when ...。
rules.en: Pair Scarcely with when. Hardly also pairs with when, whereas No sooner pairs with than.

rules.zh: 兩件事情必須幾乎緊接發生 這個句型不能用來描述相隔很久的事情。 自然： Scarcely had I sat down when the phone rang. （我剛坐下，電話便響了。） 不自然： Scarcely had I finished school when I found a job three years later. （我畢業後三年才找到工作。） 三年後並不是「幾乎立即」。
rules.en: Use the structure only for events that happen almost immediately one after the other, not events separated by a long period.

rules.zh: 第一件事情通常先完成 Scarcely had Maya locked the door when she realised that her keys were inside. 先發生： Maya locked the door. 緊接發生： She realised that her keys were inside.
rules.en: The first event is normally completed just before the second event occurs.

rules.zh: 兩部分的主語可以不同 Scarcely had the train stopped when the doors opened. ● 第一部分主語：the train ● 第二部分主語：the doors 兩個主語不需要相同，但事情的先後關係必須清楚。
rules.en: The two clauses may have different subjects as long as their sequence is clear.

rules.zh: 在這裏不是「很少」 Scarcely 有時表示「幾乎不」： I could scarcely hear him. （我幾乎聽不到他說話。） 但在 Scarcely ... when ... 中，它表示： 「剛剛……便……」
rules.en: In this pattern, Scarcely means “only just ... when ...”, not its separate meaning “hardly” or “almost not”.

rules.zh: 這個句型語氣較正式 Scarcely ... when ... 常見於： ● 故事 ● 新聞敘述 ● 正式作文 ● 事件報告 ● 描述突然發生的事情 日常口語通常更常使用 as soon as。
rules.en: The structure is relatively formal and is common in stories, news narratives, formal essays and incident reports; everyday speech more often uses as soon as.

benefits.zh: 清楚表達兩件事緊接發生 這個句型能準確表示第一件事剛剛完成，第二件事便立即發生，讓事情的先後次序十分清楚。
benefits.en: It shows that two events happened almost immediately and makes their order clear.

benefits.zh: 加強速度感或突然感 Scarcely 放在句首，會特別強調第二件事情來得很快，有時甚至令人意外。 Compare： As soon as the teacher finished speaking, the students started asking questions. （老師一說完，學生便開始發問。） Scarcely had the teacher finished speaking when the students started asking questions. （老師話音剛落，學生就開始發問。） 第二句更強調學生幾乎沒有等待，老師剛說完，他們便立即發問。
benefits.en: It adds a sense of speed or surprise by emphasising how quickly the second event occurred.

benefits.zh: 避免反覆使用 as soon as 學生在描述事情先後發生時，經常只使用 as soon as。掌握這個句型後，可以用另一種方式表達 相同關係，使文章不會過於重複。
benefits.en: It gives you another way to express “as soon as” and reduces repetition.

benefits.zh: 增加句子開頭的變化 一般句子經常以人物或事物作為主語開始： The meeting had just begun when the alarm sounded. 使用倒裝後，可以用 Scarcely 開始： Scarcely had the meeting begun when the alarm sounded. 這能讓故事和文章的句式更有變化。
benefits.en: It creates a more varied sentence opening by beginning with Scarcely instead of the subject.

benefits.zh: 適合描述接連發生的事件 這個句型很適合描述： ● 突然收到消息 ● 警報響起 ● 人群作出反應 ● 意外發生 ● 某人剛完成一件事便遇到另一件事 它可以令故事發展更加緊湊。
benefits.en: It is useful for storytelling and for describing sudden messages, alarms, reactions and accidents.

benefits.zh: 把兩件事情清楚連成一句 不用寫成兩個互不相連的短句： The train stopped. The doors opened immediately. 你可以寫成： Scarcely had the train stopped when the doors opened. 讀者能立即理解兩件事情的時間關係。
benefits.en: It combines two events clearly in one sentence so that their time relationship is immediately understood.
